question: What are Flask blueprints and how do you use them to structure a large application?
title: Flask Blueprints
direct_answer: Blueprints group related views, templates, and static files into reusable components. A Blueprint defines routes with @bp.route() instead of @app.route(). Register it with app.register_blueprint(bp, url_prefix='/prefix'). Benefits: separate files per feature area, url_for() uses blueprint names (blueprint.view_name), blueprints can be reused across projects.
interviewer_intent: Tests Flask architecture knowledge for medium-to-large applications.

seo.metaDescription: Flask blueprints for modular applications: Blueprint creation, route decoration, register_blueprint, and url_for with blueprint names.

speakable_v2.hook: Blueprints let you split a Flask app into feature modules without losing the unified routing and url_for system.

beats.content: Blueprint('users', __name__) creates a blueprint. Decorate routes with @bp.route() instead of @app.route(). Register with app.register_blueprint(bp, url_prefix='/users').
url_for uses blueprint names: url_for('users.get_user', user_id=1). The prefix is the blueprint name, not the url_prefix.

speakable_v2.cap: url_prefix can be set in register_blueprint — keep routes in the blueprint generic so the same blueprint can be mounted at different paths.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Follow up with Flask application context for accessing the database inside blueprints.
